title: Precision per-customer caching adviser & staged abortable rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a per-customer caching adviser that produces safe, customer-specific batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations plus an abortable staged rollout mechanism. The adviser will run offline simulations on historical traffic to propose conservative cache/batching config profiles per customer and per-route, expose a dry-run mode (shadow apply) and a staged canary commit system with automatic rollback triggers and an operator abort pathway. This ticket covers the end-to-end pipeline: simulation engine, scoring and recommendation UI, config commit flow (dry-run -> canary -> gradual ramp -> full commit), telemetry and rollback guardrails, and integration with allowlist/denylist and tier-based controls for customers with special policies.
acceptance_criteria: Adviser generates a ranked list of per-customer per-route cache/batching profile recommendations from historical traffic within 2 hours for a 30-day dataset (simulator offline mode)
Dry-run mode can be executed without affecting live traffic and produces a delta-cost and delta-latency projection per route/customer visible in Console
Canary commit flow supports staged rollout percentages (1%, 5%, 20%) and automatic rollback when any configured metric breach occurs
Abortable operator kill-switch that immediately reverts all active staged changes and publishes a rollback reason to the audit log
Integration honors customer allowlists and denylist rules: customers on denylist cannot be auto-tuned and will be flagged in recommendations
Tier-based policy overrides applied: enterprise-tier customers default to conservative profiles unless explicitly opted-in
End-to-end tests exercise dry-run, canary, rollback and operator abort with mock telemetry and pass in CI
Documentation in Confluence and a short Console walkthrough for SRE and Solutions Engineers are published
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype simulator: replay historical requests with control and candidate cache/batch settings to estimate token-level cost and tail-latency impact
2) Recommendation engine: score candidate profiles by cost savings vs risk (latency regression probability) and attach confidence bands
3) Policy layer: evaluate per-customer segmentation, allowlist/denylist membership and tier overrides before recommending
4) Dry-run/Shadow apply: instrument shadowed KV/batch behavior and produce simulated telemetry without affecting production paths
5) Staged commit service: orchestrate canary percentages, gradual ramps, and an operator abort endpoint with idempotent rollback
6) Telemetry & SLOs: wire up cost, p50/p95 latency, error rate, and user-perceived regressions to rollback rules
7) Console UI: surface recommendations, confidence, simulation outputs, and one-click staging (dry-run -> canary)
8) E2E tests and runbook: automated tests, rollback playbook, and on-call runbook for incidents
rollback_conditions: p95 latency increase > 20% relative to baseline for the canary cohort
error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points over baseline
user-facing failure rate increased by more than 0.25 percentage points
cache hit ratio drops below projected lower confidence bound
operator manual abort via Console or API
